correctness.rationale: With known q>alpha>b, p=psi is recovered exactly as R/(1+R) from covariance and margins, then alpha,b,delta recover by algebra; all four probabilities are positive in the model. At q=1 the full 3-parameter Fisher determinant equals (1-p)t^2 exp(-delta*t)/(p+(1-p)alpha^2 exp(-delta*t)). The log derivative is 2/z-1/(1+C*exp(-z)), a strictly decreasing function crossing zero exactly once, so the unique global optimum is z=2+W(2*C*exp(-2)). Endpoint objective limits are zero. Monotonicity and p->0 asymptotic follow from monotonic W and its standard large-argument expansion. Replayed deterministic checker using rational exact mixture and Fisher identities: PASS exact_fraction_checks=1296 numeric_checks=2415. Finite checks supplement, not prove, the universal result.

value.rationale: Persistence of ecological evidence after organisms disappear makes binary positives an imperfect proxy for living occupancy. The explicit two-date identification of occupancy, residual detection level and residual decay rate is a meaningful structural inference statement. A unique revisit-time information optimum beyond two decay times and its logarithmically increasing rare-occupancy law expose real design tradeoffs missing from single-date or static false-positive models. Applied interpretation is a benchmark only; fixed status, perfectly calibrated detector in the timing theorem, independent Bernoulli outcomes, exponential binary probability decay and no delay costs sharply delimit validity.
